item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez

item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: Here's a question straight out of sci-fi: What if AI could predict what you were going to do before you decided to, even in a completely new situation?

item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz

item.title: Here’s what ‘renoa’ — the first new fiber in 25 years — feels like
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Startup Everbloom's new material, renoa, is the first new fiber in 25 years, and it feels very familiar.

item.title: Salesforce’s M&A spree continues with a reported $375M deal for defense tech startup Rune
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: The AI logistics startup will bolster the CRM giant's Missionforce defense platform.

item.title: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: As an increasing number of AI assistants flood the market, the founder of Ollie, an assistant that respected its users' privacy, says it will be shutting down in a week.

item.title: AI law firm Crosby bids on disintegrating, famed firm Weil Gotshal
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Like a real-life episode of "Suits," the demise of famed white-shoe Wall Street law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges has been the talk of the legal industry. And now an AI firm has entered the picture.

item.title: Satlyt takes another step toward turning satellites into space data centers
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Satlyt ran a successful test this month bringing it closer to turning spacecraft, starting with satellites, into virtual data centers.

item.title: Zest’s new AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations over text
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Can't agree on where to eat? Zest's AI concierge can combine everyone's tastes, put restaurant options to a vote, and make the reservation.

item.dc:creator: TechCrunch Events

item.title: Can AI data centers be mass-produced like cars? This startup aims to find out
item.dc:creator: Dominic-Madori Davis
item.description: Runware is building a factory to turn out prefabricated AI data centers on an assembly line. The real test will be whether it can deliver at that scale.

item.title: Ex-Palantir execs launch Dream with $17M from a16z to build AI world models for construction
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Dream is grounded in real physics and construction standards. Just as LLMs learn from text, Dream's world model is trained on more than 100 million square feet of building data gathered from permit archives across the United States.

item.title: Agent identity startup Mintive lands Cowboy Ventures, Coatue, angels Jeff Dean, Andrej Karpathy
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Mintive was founded by two engineers who have been working on AI for decades through Google Brain and Coursera. It's platform promises to help IT easily control enterprise agents.
